html:
SMTO-GWT-0002 — Gateway unavailable

GUID: ff8a4eef-6559-470f-945d-eabbe6cb2aea
Slug: gateway-unavailable
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't reach the computer chosen for this task, so it stopped before sending the next step there. Steps sent before this check may already have run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on the Gateway this task uses. Read its status and the Last check message. The status tells you whether SMTO can't reach the computer or doesn't trust it anymore.
  2. If it says Connection failed, make sure that computer is switched on, connected to the network, and its Gateway program is running. Then select Check connection again. SMTO only starts the task once the computer answers this check.
  3. If the row shows an Identity changed badge, ask the person who manages that computer whether its Gateway was reinstalled. Don't forget the old identity unless they confirm it. A changed identity can mean a different computer is answering at that address.
  4. When the row shows Connected, look at the task's earlier steps to see what already ran on that computer. Then run the task again. The step that failed this check wasn't sent, but steps before it may have finished, and repeating them could do the work twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's row shows Connected and the task starts running its steps.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer. Don't turn off security checks or point the task at a different computer to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway connection check (at the start of a run, or before a later step was sent) found the selected Gateway unavailable: disabled, unreachable, or its trusted identity changed. The step being checked was not sent, but earlier steps may already have run.

What this means

  • The runtime could not communicate with the selected Gateway. It may be offline, disabled, misconfigured or unreachable from the runtime; the current connection state distinguishes these possibilities. This availability error does not settle the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The selected Gateway has no usable connection from the runtime. Service state, selection and network reachability require separate checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the selected Gateway and its connection status in Mission Control. Ask its operator to confirm the service is running on the expected endpoint; for prior dispatched work, inspect the saved receipt and current state.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway record's status and last_error with a health check; failure_category is gateway_unreachable or gateway_identity_changed. Restore network reachability and the Gateway process, or resolve a TLS identity change through re-enrollment only after verifying the host; confirm the outcome of steps already dispatched in this run (and earlier runs) from their receipts before repeating them.
  • Check the selected Gateway’s connection status and configured endpoint in Mission Control. Restore the connection, then reconcile any previously dispatched operation before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended Gateway reports its identity and supported capabilities; outstanding work has a known receipt or remains explicitly unresolved.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Availability or connection failure does not establish nonexecution for a previously dispatched operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
